description: 1S5F is a team composed of 1st Year BS Computer Science students at the University of the Philippines - Mindanao. Recognizing the great potential of NASA data to make something functional, 1S5F aims to help achieve that and harness the data into a functioning software that aims to produce real-life solutions to problems that exists beyond the skies.
summary:
Vital Indicators Tracking for Astronaut Life (VITAL) is an astronaut health-monitoring platform that brings vital signs, blood test results, and radiation measurements into one dashboard. It compares recorded readings with preflight baselines and documented reference ranges, highlights alerts, and lets crew members review trends and ask Orbit, the AI health companion, for explanations.

The project addresses the challenge of helping crews and mission teams monitor health during long-duration spaceflight, where access to Earth-based medical care is limited. Bringing these measurements together can help make changes and potential concerns easier to spot and discuss with medical professionals.
details:
VITAL is a health-monitoring dashboard for astronaut crews. It brings together vital signs, blood-analysis results, and physical and biological radiation measurements, then compares available readings with preflight baselines and reference ranges. The dashboard highlights results that may need attention, shows measurement history, and lets crew members ask Orbit, an AI health companion, for plain-language explanations.

The software uses a web interface built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with a Node.js and TypeScript backend and Supabase/SQLite data support. It can display sample records and accept blood-result spreadsheets. The concept also explores a standalone monitoring station that could house vital-sign sensors, a sample-analysis unit, and radiation-monitoring equipment.

The team considered two key factors in developing the proposed solution: first, how crew members onboard can conveniently log into the system, input, and submit their health information; and second, how administrators can remotely access, monitor, and assess the crew's health status throughout the duration of their mission. The first factor was solved through incorporating hardware mechanisms to fetch data. Logging in was made convenient through the use of NFC cards, containing the identities of the crew members onboard, while the health information can be inputted and submitted through getting a blood sample of the crew on a slide and allowing the sensors on the machine to read the data for the software to read, compare, analyze, and display data. The second factor was resolved through connecting the remote device to a mainframe computer to allow the administrative personnel to assess their health while on a mission and to allow communication between the crew on a mission and the ground personnel.

By bringing several types of health information into one place, VITAL aims to help crew and medical teams review trends and notice potential concerns during missions where immediate access to Earth-based care is limited. Our longer-term goal is to develop the concept into a reliable, space-compatible system that supports informed medical decisions.

Use of Artificial Intelligence

We used AI tools to assist with development, research, and communication. Large language models helped us review code, refine dashboard copy, reason through reference range and alert logic, and troubleshoot implementation issues. Image generation helped us visualize a standalone health-monitoring station and its components. Listed below are the super intelligence used by the team.

  • ChatGPT (OpenAI): Assisted with code review, troubleshooting, dashboard wording, and organizing the alert logic.
  • AI image generation (Codex): Created concept illustrations of the standalone astronaut health-monitoring station.
  • AI coding assistance (Github Copilot, Codex, Claude): Helped explain implementation options and refine frontend and backend code.
  • ChatGPT (OpenAI): Assisted with code review, troubleshooting, dashboard wording, and organizing the alert logic.
  • Gemini Notebook: Assisted with research and data gathering for specifying the parameters that are used within the software.

The project direction and intended use came from our team. AI tools supported our work, but the dashboard’s health information is a prototype and does not provide a medical diagnosis.
